name: Wingspan
notes: Attract birds to your preserves and build an engine that gets stronger every round. Relaxed pace with plenty to think about.

name: Wingspan: Oceania Expansion
notes: Adds Oceania birds, nectar as a new food, and new player boards. Requires the base game.

name: Wingspan: European Expansion
notes: Adds European birds with new powers and a deck of end-of-round goals. Requires the base game.

name: Wingspan Asia
notes: Plays on its own for 1–2 players, or combines with base Wingspan for up to 7.

name: Pandemic
notes: Work together to treat four diseases before outbreaks spread out of control. Everyone wins or loses as a team.

name: Pandemic: On the Brink
notes: Adds new roles, tougher challenges, and room for a fifth player. Requires the base game.

name: Abducktion
notes: Rearrange plastic ducks into patterns so an alien UFO can beam them up. Takes about two minutes to learn.

name: Abducktion: IntergalacDuck Research Expansion
notes: Adds research pods, harder patterns, and room for up to six players. Requires the base game.

name: Harry Potter: Hogwarts Battle
notes: Team up as Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Neville, building decks to fight off villains. Seven unlockable years ramp up the difficulty.

name: Harry Potter: Hogwarts Battle: The Monster Box of Monsters
notes: Adds Luna Lovegood as a fifth hero, plus creatures, encounters, and detention cards. Requires the base game.

name: Smash Up
notes: Pick two factions, shuffle them into one deck, and fight for control of bases. This collection includes every set below, stored together in one box.

name: Smash Up: Core Set
notes: The original set, with Aliens, Dinosaurs, Ninjas, Pirates, Robots, Tricksters, Wizards, and Zombies. Plays on its own.

name: Smash Up: Awesome Level 9000
notes: Adds Bear Cavalry, Ghosts, Killer Plants, and Steampunks.

name: Smash Up: Science Fiction Double Feature
notes: Adds Cyborg Apes, Shapeshifters, Super Spies, and Time Travelers.

name: Pretty Pretty Smash Up
notes: Adds Fairies, Kitty Cats, Mythic Horses, and Princesses.

name: Smash Up: It's Your Fault!
notes: Adds Dragons, Mythic Greeks, Sharks, Superheroes, and the bonus Tornadoes faction.

name: Smash Up: Cease and Desist
notes: Adds Astroknights, Changerbots, Ignobles, and Star Roamers.

name: Smash Up: Big in Japan
notes: Adds Itty Critters, Kaiju, Magical Girls, and Mega Troopers.

name: Smash Up: World Tour: International Incident
notes: Adds Luchadores, Mounties, Musketeers, and Sumo Wrestlers.

name: Smash Up: The Bigger Geekier Box
notes: Adds the Geeks and All-Stars factions, plus the box that holds the whole collection and the complete rulebook.

name: Smash Up: Disney Edition
notes: A standalone set with eight Disney factions, from Frozen to The Nightmare Before Christmas.

name: Smash Up: Munchkin
notes: A standalone set that adds monsters to fight and treasure to win. Mixing it in changes how every game plays.

name: Smash Up: Marvel
notes: A standalone set with Marvel hero and villain factions.

name: Pandemic Legacy: Season 1
notes: A Pandemic campaign where every game permanently changes the board. This campaign is four months in, and new players can join at any point.

name: Ticket to Ride
notes: Collect train cards and claim routes across North America. One of the easiest big games to teach.

name: Ticket to Ride: Europe
notes: Claim routes across Europe, with tunnels, ferries, and train stations. Still sealed and ready for its first game.

name: Catan
notes: Trade resources and build roads and settlements across the island. Expect plenty of bargaining.

name: Catan: 5–6 Player Extension
notes: Adds the pieces and tiles for a fifth and sixth player. Requires the base game.

name: Catan: Starfarers
notes: Fly ships through space, trade with alien civilizations, and found colonies. A longer, bigger take on Catan.

name: 7 Wonders Duel
notes: Draft cards to build a civilization and race to one of three ways to win. A two-player game.

name: Sky Team
notes: Land a plane together without talking, using dice to work the controls. A two-player game.

name: King of Tokyo
notes: Roll dice as giant monsters and battle for control of Tokyo. Fast, loud, and easy to teach.

name: Parks
notes: Hike trails through four seasons, collecting tokens to visit national parks. Beautiful art and a relaxed pace.

name: Forbidden Desert
notes: Work together to dig up a lost flying machine before the sandstorm buries the team. Everyone wins or loses together.

name: Harry Potter: Hogwarts Battle: Defence Against the Dark Arts
notes: Duel head to head, building a deck of spells to stun your opponent. A two-player game.

name: Hive
notes: Place and move bug tiles to surround the opposing queen. A two-player game with no board.

name: Mysterium
notes: One player is a silent ghost sending dream cards, and everyone else works out the murder from the clues. Works well with a big group.

name: Arkham Horror: The Card Game
notes: Investigate cosmic horror through a story campaign, building decks along the way. A two-player game, and the heaviest on the shelf.

name: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game
notes: Quest through Middle-earth together, building decks of heroes and allies. A two-player game.

name: Rick and Morty: Anatomy Park
notes: Build a theme park inside a human body while diseases break loose. Based on the Rick and Morty episode, with adult humor.

name: Back to the Future: Back in Time
notes: Work together to fix the DeLorean and get Marty's parents together before 10:04 pm. Tough to win the first few times.

name: Jurassic Park: Danger!
notes: One player controls the dinosaurs while everyone else tries to escape Isla Nublar. Based on the original movie.

name: Clue: Treachery at Tudor Mansion
notes: Explore a mansion escape-room style, then solve a Clue mystery with what you find. Can only be played once.

name: Qwirkle
notes: Match colors and shapes to build rows of tiles. Simple rules with real strategy.

name: Qwirkle Rummy
notes: Build sets of matching shapes or colors, rummy style. The card version of Qwirkle.

name: Codenames
notes: Split into two teams and give one-word clues to find your agents. Works well with a big group.

name: Telestrations: 6 Player Family Pack
notes: Draw a word, pass it on, and guess what the next person drew. Telephone with sketchbooks.

name: Horrible Therapist
notes: Build three-panel therapy comics from question, answer, and treatment cards. Adults only.

name: Tapple
notes: Name something in the category, tap the letter, and beat the timer. Quick rounds for any size group.

name: Sequence
notes: Play cards to place chips and make rows of five. Plays best in teams.

name: HISTORY Channel Trivia Game
notes: Answer questions across five categories, from science to sports. There are two copies, so two tables can play at once.

name: Risk
notes: Build armies and conquer the world one territory at a time. Plan on a long night.

name: Monopoly
notes: Buy properties, collect rent, and bankrupt everyone else. The classic.

name: Battleship
notes: Hide a fleet and call shots to sink the other side's ships. A two-player game.

name: Stratego
notes: Hide your army's ranks and capture the enemy flag. A two-player game.

name: Yahtzee
notes: Roll five dice and fill the scorecard with the best combinations. Quick and easy for any group.

name: Flip 7
notes: Flip cards one at a time and stop before you draw a duplicate. Quick push-your-luck fun for any size group.

name: Crazy Nines
notes: Swap and flip cards to keep your score as low as possible over nine holes. Plays like golf.

name: Jenga
notes: Pull a block, stack it on top, and don't be the one who topples the tower. A good break between bigger games.

name: The Mind
notes: Play numbered cards in rising order as a team, without saying a word. Simple to learn and surprisingly tense.

name: Magical Athlete
notes: Draft a team of racers with game-breaking powers, then roll dice to race them over four rounds. Chaotic and quick to learn.
